# Purpose

`survival.qmd` (Phase 1b) estimates each state's net used-vehicle import rate from state-vs-national survival differences (Greene/UTK method). It reports the rate with national-survival weights. Its vehicle counts come from **age-mix accounting**: each state's age 2-8 survivors minus what national survival would leave from its own year-*t* stock, age by age. These counts sum to exactly zero nationally in every yearpair. Part of that net flow is simply vehicles travelling with people who move between states. This document:

1. parses the Census Bureau's ACS state-to-state migration flow tables into a tidy origin × destination × year table;
2. builds per-state population inflow, outflow and net domestic migration (persons and % of population), with Sankeys in the same style as the vehicle ones;
3. aligns ACS years to vehicle yearpairs;
4. estimates **A**, the number of age 2-8 vehicles of a class that move per net migrant, in two transparent ways (structural per-capita fleet; empirical regression slope);
5. removes `A × net domestic migration` from vehicle net imports, giving population-adjusted ("market") flows, with Sankeys, ranking comparisons and the share of vehicle net-flow variation that population migration accounts for.

Vehicle inputs are the CSVs `survival.qmd` writes, using the `old` (national-survival weights) method, the production method:

- `data/net_imports_agemix_counts.csv`: vehicle counts.
- `data/net_imports_long.csv`: the weighted rates used for % labels.
- `data/state_vehtype_stock_by_year.csv`: age 2-8 stock, for per-capita A and the % bases.
- `data/net_imports_summary.csv`: full-window reference values, including `Average_agemix`.

The age-mix counts and `Average_agemix` are written by the `survival.qmd` version on PR #3. This document does not run any `survival.qmd` chunk. Outputs go to the git-ignored `est net flows/population/`.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(networkD3)
library(ggrepel)

# htmlwidgets::saveWidget(selfcontained = TRUE) needs pandoc; under plain
# Rscript it is not on the path, so point it at RStudio's bundled copy
pandoc_dir <- "C:/Program Files/RStudio/resources/app/bin/quarto/bin/tools"
if (dir.exists(pandoc_dir)) Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PANDOC = pandoc_dir)

census_dir    <- here::here("data", "raw", "census_state_to_state")
surv_data_dir <- here::here("data")
rel_out_dir   <- file.path("est net flows", "population")
out_dir       <- here::here(rel_out_dir)
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

states51 <- sort(c(state.name, "District of Columbia"))
classes  <- c("Car", "SUV", "Pickup")

# vehicle averaging windows, start-year labels (2014 = yearpair 2014/15);
# same definitions as survival.qmd's netimports-summaries chunk
year_sets <- list(
  yrs1519  = 2015:2019,
  yrs1421  = 2014:2021,
  yrs_excl = setdiff(2014:2024, c(2020, 2022)),
  yrs_all  = 2014:2024
)
year_set_labels <- c(
  yrs1519  = "2015/16–2019/20",
  yrs1421  = "2014/15–2021/22",
  yrs_excl = "2014/15–2024/25 excl. 20/21 & 22/23",
  yrs_all  = "2014/15–2024/25 (all)"
)
window_years <- imap(year_sets, \(yrs, nm) tibble(year_set = nm, year = yrs)) |>
  list_rbind()

yp_label <- function(year) paste0(year, "/", str_sub(year + 1, 3, 4))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  plot.title.position = "plot"))
col_exp <- "#7b2d8e"   # exporter purple, as in the Sankeys
col_imp <- "#e67e22"   # importer orange
```

# Census state-to-state migration data

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, [State-to-State Migration Flows](https://www.census.gov/data/tables/time-series/demo/geographic-mobility/state-to-state-migration.html), ACS 1-year estimates, one Excel file per year, saved unmodified under `data/raw/census_state_to_state/`.

- **Coverage.** ACS 2014–2019 and 2021–2024 were downloaded. 2014 is not matched to a vehicle yearpair under the alignment below; it is used only for the alignment check. Alaska's ACS 2014 out-migration (93k, against ~40k in every other year) fails the screen in *Population statistics* and is excluded as anomalous, although Census documents no error for it.
- **2020 gap.** The Census Bureau did not release standard ACS 2020 1-year tables (pandemic data-collection disruption), so there is no 2020 state-to-state table. The directory `…/geographic-mobility/2020/state-to-state-migration/` returns 404.
- **2025 gap.** ACS 2025 flows were not yet published when the files were downloaded (14 Oct 2026); `…/2025/state-to-state-migration/` also returns 404.
- **2022 Connecticut error.** The 2022 file (`…_updated_2024_06_27.xlsx`) is the current Census version, but Census still flags a processing error for respondents who moved within Connecticut or out of it. Census advises not comparing Connecticut's 2022 flows with other years, and using caution with other states for 2022; the error was fixed only from the 2023 release on. In the file, CT's 2022 in-migrants (145k) are ~50% above 2021/2023 and its within-state movers are correspondingly low, so some within-CT moves were coded as moves from other states. **Connecticut ACS 2022 (vehicle yearpair 2021/22) is excluded** from all population statistics, Sankeys, regressions and adjustments below. The spill-over onto other states' 2022 out-migration is quantified below.
- **2024 format change.** The 2024 file switched to a long table plus two supplemental sheets. It also suppresses 285 small origin–destination cells as "N" (too few sample cases). Older years have no suppression.

```{r census-files}
census_files <- tibble(file = list.files(census_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx?$")) |>
  mutate(acs_year = as.integer(str_extract(file, "(?<=Table_)\\d{4}")),
         size_kb  = round(file.size(file.path(census_dir, file)) / 1024),
         layout   = if_else(acs_year >= 2024, "long + supplemental totals",
                            "wide matrix")) |>
  arrange(acs_year)
knitr::kable(census_files, caption = "Downloaded ACS state-to-state migration tables")
```

## Parsing

All years cross-tabulate *current residence* (rows) against *residence 1 year ago* (columns), with an estimate and a 90% margin of error (MOE) for each cell. Universe: population 1 year and over. The layouts differ:

- **2014–2022:** a wide matrix split into two row blocks, each with its own header (rows 6–8 and 45–47). The row-header column repeats every 11 columns.
- **2023:** one header block (rows 5–8) and one row-header column.
- **2024:** long format (current residence, residence 1 year ago, estimate, MOE). In-migrant and out-migrant totals and population are on separate supplemental sheets.

Columns are identified by their header text, never by position, so all three layouts go through the same item classifier.

```{r census-parse}
# header/row labels carry footnote digits ("United States2", "U.S. Island
# Area3") and embedded line breaks
clean_label <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("[\r\n]+", " ") |>
    str_squish() |>
    str_remove("\\d+$")
}

geo_rows <- c("United States", states51, "Puerto Rico")
abroad_parts <- c("Puerto Rico", "U.S. Island Areas", "Foreign country")

# header label (+ its group label) -> one item code shared by all layouts
classify_item <- function(lab, group) {
  case_when(
    str_detect(lab, "^Population 1 year and over$")  ~ "pop_1yr_plus",
    str_detect(lab, "^Same (house|residence)")       ~ "same_house",
    str_detect(lab, "^Same state")                   ~ "same_state",
    lab == "Total" & str_detect(group, "^Different") ~ "in_diff_state_total",
    lab == "Total" & str_detect(group, "^Abroad")    ~ "abroad_total",
    lab %in% states51                                ~ lab,
    lab == "Puerto Rico"                             ~ "Puerto Rico",
    str_detect(lab, "^U\\.S\\. Island Area")         ~ "U.S. Island Areas",
    str_detect(lab, "(?i)^Foreign country")          ~ "Foreign country",
    .default = NA_character_
  )
}

read_text_matrix <- function(path, sheet = 1) {
  read_excel(path, sheet = sheet, col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text",
             .name_repair = ~ paste0("c", seq_along(.x))) |>
    as.matrix()
}

# 2014-2023: wide matrix; each header block ends in a row of
# "Estimate"/"MOE" pairs, with origin labels in the 1-3 rows above it
parse_wide <- function(path, acs_year) {
  m <- read_text_matrix(path)
  row_lab   <- clean_label(m[, 1])
  data_rows <- which(row_lab %in% geo_rows)
  est_rows  <- which(apply(m, 1, \(r) any(r %in% "Estimate")))

  col_maps <- map(est_rows, \(h) {
    hdr_rows <- setdiff((h - 3):(h - 1), data_rows)
    est_cols <- which(m[h, ] %in% "Estimate")
    stopifnot(all(str_detect(m[h, est_cols + 1], "^(MOE|Margin)")))
    tibble(
      est_col = est_cols,
      # the label nearest the Estimate row: state name or "Total" where
      # present, else the group label ("Population 1 year and over", ...)
      lab = map_chr(est_cols, \(j) {
        v <- m[hdr_rows, j]
        v <- v[!is.na(v)]
        if (length(v)) clean_label(v[length(v)]) else NA_character_
      }),
      group = clean_label(m[h - 2, est_cols]) |> replace_na("")
    ) |>
      mutate(item = classify_item(lab, group))
  }) |>
    set_names(est_rows)

  map(data_rows, \(r) {
    cm <- col_maps[[as.character(max(est_rows[est_rows < r]))]]
    stopifnot(!anyNA(cm$item))
    tibble(acs_year = acs_year,
           dest     = row_lab[r],
           item     = cm$item,
           est_raw  = m[r, cm$est_col],
           moe_raw  = m[r, cm$est_col + 1])
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
}

# 2024: long origin-destination table + supplemental total sheets
parse_long <- function(path, acs_year) {
  t1 <- read_text_matrix(path, sheet = "Table")
  stopifnot(str_detect(t1[8, 3], "^Estimate"), str_detect(t1[8, 4], "^Margin"))
  od <- tibble(acs_year = acs_year,
               dest     = clean_label(t1[, 1]),
               item     = classify_item(clean_label(t1[, 2]), ""),
               est_raw  = t1[, 3],
               moe_raw  = t1[, 4]) |>
    filter(dest %in% geo_rows, !is.na(item))

  read_supp <- function(sheet, codes) {
    s <- read_text_matrix(path, sheet = sheet)
    h <- which(apply(s, 1, \(r) any(r %in% "Estimate")))[1]
    est_cols <- which(s[h, ] %in% "Estimate")
    labs <- clean_label(s[5, est_cols])
    item <- codes[map_int(labs, \(l) which(str_detect(l, names(codes)))[1])]
    stopifnot(!anyNA(item))
    rows <- which(clean_label(s[, 1]) %in% geo_rows)
    map(rows, \(r) tibble(acs_year = acs_year,
                          dest     = clean_label(s[r, 1]),
                          item     = unname(item),
                          est_raw  = s[r, est_cols],
                          moe_raw  = s[r, est_cols + 1])) |>
      list_rbind()
  }
  supp_cur <- read_supp("Supplemental - Current Res", c(
    "^Population 1 year and over$" = "pop_1yr_plus",
    "with same residence"          = "same_house",
    "within same state"            = "same_state",
    "from different state"         = "in_diff_state_total",
    "from abroad"                  = "abroad_total"))
  # "dest" here is the state of residence 1 year ago
  supp_ago <- read_supp("Supplemental - Res 1 Year Ago", c(
    "^Population living in state"  = "pop_1yr_ago",
    "with same residence"          = "same_house_ago",
    "within same state"            = "same_state_ago",
    "to different state"           = "out_diff_state_total")) |>
    filter(item %in% c("pop_1yr_ago", "out_diff_state_total"))
  bind_rows(od, supp_cur, supp_ago)
}

census_raw <- census_files |>
  select(file, acs_year) |>
  pmap(\(file, acs_year) {
    path <- file.path(census_dir, file)
    if (acs_year >= 2024) parse_long(path, acs_year) else parse_wide(path, acs_year)
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  # "N/A"/"X" = not applicable (own state); "N" = suppressed, too few cases
  mutate(suppressed = est_raw %in% "N",
         estimate   = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(est_raw)),
         moe        = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(moe_raw)))

# any non-numeric code other than the documented ones would be a parse error
stopifnot(census_raw |>
            filter(!is.na(est_raw), is.na(estimate)) |>
            pull(est_raw) |>
            str_detect("^(N/A\\d*|N|X)$") |>
            all())

# tidy origin x destination flows (destination = current residence)
census_flows <- census_raw |>
  filter(item %in% c(states51, abroad_parts), dest != "United States") |>
  transmute(acs_year,
            origin = item,
            dest,
            origin_type = if_else(origin %in% states51, "state", origin),
            dest_type   = if_else(dest %in% states51, "state", dest),
            estimate, moe, suppressed) |>
  filter(origin != dest)

census_totals <- census_raw |>
  filter(!item %in% c(states51, abroad_parts)) |>
  select(acs_year, geo = dest, item, estimate, moe)

write_csv(census_flows,  file.path(out_dir, "census_state_to_state_flows.csv"))
write_csv(census_totals, file.path(out_dir, "census_state_totals.csv"))
```

## Checks

```{r census-checks}
dom <- census_flows |> filter(origin_type == "state", dest_type == "state")

# matrix row sums vs published "different state" in-migrant totals; the 2024
# gap is the suppressed cells
chk <- dom |>
  summarise(in_matrix = sum(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_suppressed = sum(suppressed),
            .by = c(acs_year, dest)) |>
  left_join(census_totals |>
              filter(item == "in_diff_state_total") |>
              select(acs_year, dest = geo, in_published = estimate),
            by = join_by(acs_year, dest)) |>
  summarise(states = n(),
            max_abs_diff = max(abs(in_matrix - in_published)),
            movers_in_suppressed_cells = sum(in_published - in_matrix),
            n_suppressed_cells = sum(n_suppressed),
            .by = acs_year) |>
  left_join(census_totals |>
              filter(geo == "United States", item == "in_diff_state_total") |>
              select(acs_year, us_interstate_movers = estimate),
            by = join_by(acs_year)) |>
  arrange(acs_year)

stopifnot(chk |> filter(acs_year < 2024) |> pull(max_abs_diff) |> max() == 0)
knitr::kable(chk |> mutate(acs_year = as.character(acs_year)),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "Origin-destination row sums vs published in-migrant totals (50 states + DC)")
```

In every year before 2024, the matrix reproduces the published in-migrant totals exactly. In 2024, `r chk |> filter(acs_year == 2024) |> pull(n_suppressed_cells)` suppressed domestic cells hide `r scales::comma(chk |> filter(acs_year == 2024) |> pull(movers_in_suppressed_cells))` movers (`r scales::percent(chk |> filter(acs_year == 2024) |> with(movers_in_suppressed_cells / us_interstate_movers), accuracy = 0.1)` of interstate movers). The 2024 supplemental sheets give complete in- and out-migrant totals per state, so 2024 state totals come from them. Origin–destination detail is used only where suppression does not matter.

# Population statistics

Per state and ACS year, for domestic interstate moves among the 50 states and DC:

- **inflow**: persons who lived in another state 1 year ago (published total).
- **outflow**: persons who lived in this state 1 year ago and now live in another state. This is the column sum of the matrix, or the supplemental total in 2024.
- **net** = inflow − outflow. It sums to zero across states every year.
- **net rate** = net / state population age 1+ (current residence, same table).

MOEs for sums use the Census approximation $\sqrt{\sum MOE^2}$, ignoring covariance, so they are approximate.

Moves to and from Puerto Rico and from abroad are kept separate. ACS cannot measure emigration from the US. The PR row of the table, from the Puerto Rico Community Survey, gives moves from each state to PR.

```{r pop-stats}
pop_tot <- census_totals |>
  filter(geo %in% states51) |>
  select(acs_year, statename = geo, item, estimate, moe) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = item, values_from = c(estimate, moe), names_glue = "{item}_{.value}")

outflow_matrix <- dom |>
  rename(statename = origin) |>
  summarise(outflow_matrix = sum(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
            outflow_matrix_moe = sqrt(sum(moe^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .by = c(acs_year, statename))

abroad_in <- census_flows |>
  filter(origin_type != "state", dest_type == "state") |>
  select(acs_year, statename = dest, origin, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = origin, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(from_pr = `Puerto Rico`, from_island = `U.S. Island Areas`,
         from_foreign = `Foreign country`)

to_pr <- census_flows |>
  filter(dest == "Puerto Rico", origin_type == "state") |>
  select(acs_year, statename = origin, to_pr = estimate)

pop_state_year <- pop_tot |>
  left_join(outflow_matrix, by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
  left_join(abroad_in, by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
  left_join(to_pr, by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
  transmute(
    acs_year, statename,
    pop         = pop_1yr_plus_estimate,
    inflow      = in_diff_state_total_estimate,
    inflow_moe  = in_diff_state_total_moe,
    # 2024: matrix has suppressed cells, use the complete supplemental total
    outflow     = if_else(acs_year >= 2024, out_diff_state_total_estimate, outflow_matrix),
    outflow_moe = if_else(acs_year >= 2024, out_diff_state_total_moe, outflow_matrix_moe),
    net         = inflow - outflow,
    net_moe     = sqrt(inflow_moe^2 + outflow_moe^2),
    net_rate    = net / pop,
    from_abroad = abroad_total_estimate,
    from_pr, from_island, from_foreign, to_pr
  ) |>
  arrange(acs_year, statename)

net_balance <- pop_state_year |> summarise(net = sum(net), .by = acs_year)
stopifnot(all(abs(net_balance$net) < 1))

# screen: state-years whose in- or out-migration is far from the state's own
# median year
flow_screen <- pop_state_year |>
  mutate(in_vs_median  = inflow / median(inflow),
         out_vs_median = outflow / median(outflow),
         .by = statename) |>
  filter(pmax(in_vs_median, out_vs_median) > 1.6 | pmin(in_vs_median, out_vs_median) < 0.6)

# flagged state-years: kept in the CSV with the reason, dropped from analysis
census_flags <- tribble(
  ~acs_year, ~statename, ~flag,
  2022L, "Connecticut", "Census: 2022 processing error for moves within/out of CT; do not compare with other years",
  2014L, "Alaska",      "Anomalous: outflow 2.2x the state's median year (not a Census-documented error)"
)
stopifnot(setequal(paste(flow_screen$acs_year, flow_screen$statename),
                   paste(census_flags$acs_year, census_flags$statename)))
pop_state_year <- pop_state_year |>
  left_join(census_flags, by = join_by(acs_year, statename))
pop_use <- pop_state_year |> filter(is.na(flag))

write_csv(pop_state_year, file.path(out_dir, "population_net_migration_by_state_year.csv"))

knitr::kable(flow_screen |>
               select(acs_year, statename, inflow, outflow, in_vs_median, out_vs_median) |>
               left_join(census_flags, by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
               mutate(acs_year = as.character(acs_year)),
             digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "State-years whose in- or out-migration is more than 1.6x or less than 0.6x the state's median year; both are excluded from analysis")

national_pop <- pop_state_year |>
  summarise(pop = sum(pop), interstate_movers = sum(inflow),
            from_abroad_foreign = sum(from_foreign, na.rm = TRUE),
            from_pr = sum(from_pr, na.rm = TRUE),
            to_pr = sum(to_pr, na.rm = TRUE),
            gross_net_in = sum(pmax(net, 0)),
            .by = acs_year)
knitr::kable(national_pop |> mutate(acs_year = as.character(acs_year)),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "National totals (50 states + DC, all states incl. flagged). gross_net_in = sum of positive state net migration (= sum of negative), i.e. the total Sankey width.")
```

The Connecticut 2022 error also touches other states. Misattributed in-migrants to CT appear as 2022 out-migrants from the state they were coded to. The table compares 2022 flows into CT from each origin with the mean of 2021 and 2023. The excess is the most those origins' 2022 outflows can be overstated by the CT error.

```{r ct-2022-check}
ct_excess <- dom |>
  filter(dest == "Connecticut", acs_year %in% 2021:2023) |>
  select(acs_year, origin, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = acs_year, values_from = estimate, names_prefix = "y") |>
  mutate(excess_2022 = y2022 - (y2021 + y2023) / 2) |>
  left_join(pop_state_year |> filter(acs_year == 2022) |> select(origin = statename, outflow, net),
            by = join_by(origin)) |>
  mutate(excess_share_of_outflow = excess_2022 / outflow) |>
  arrange(desc(excess_2022))
knitr::kable(head(ct_excess, 8) |> select(-net), digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = paste0("2022 in-migration to Connecticut by origin vs mean of 2021 and 2023; total excess ",
                              scales::comma(sum(ct_excess$excess_2022))))
```

Those origins' 2022 values are kept: the excess is at most `r scales::percent(max(ct_excess$excess_share_of_outflow, na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 0.1)` of any state's 2022 out-migration.

```{r pop-heatmap, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 11}
state_order <- pop_use |>
  summarise(r = mean(net_rate), .by = statename) |>
  arrange(r) |>
  pull(statename)

p_heat <- pop_state_year |>
  mutate(statename = factor(statename, levels = state_order),
         net_rate  = if_else(is.na(flag), net_rate, NA_real_)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(acs_year), statename, fill = net_rate)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(is.na(net_rate), "excl.",
                                scales::number(100 * net_rate, accuracy = 0.1))),
            size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = col_exp, mid = "white", high = col_imp,
                       limits = c(-0.02, 0.02), oob = scales::squish, na.value = "grey85",
                       labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 0.5),
                       name = "Net domestic\nmigration\n(% of pop.)") +
  labs(x = "ACS year (moves over the preceding ~12 months)", y = NULL,
       title = "Net domestic migration rate by state and ACS year",
       subtitle = "ACS 1-year state-to-state flows, 50 states + DC; no ACS 2020 release; flagged state-years (CT 2022, AK 2014) excluded") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "fig_population_net_rate_heatmap.png"), p_heat,
       width = 9, height = 11, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
p_heat
```

```{r pop-abroad, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
p_abroad <- national_pop |>
  select(acs_year, `Interstate movers (gross)` = interstate_movers,
         `Sum of state net gains` = gross_net_in,
         `From foreign country` = from_abroad_foreign,
         `Puerto Rico -> states` = from_pr, `States -> Puerto Rico` = to_pr) |>
  # explicit NA year so lines break at the missing ACS 2020
  complete(acs_year = 2014:2024) |>
  pivot_longer(-acs_year) |>
  mutate(name = fct_inorder(name)) |>
  ggplot(aes(acs_year, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) + geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), trans = "log10") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2024) +
  labs(x = "ACS year", y = "Persons (log scale)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Domestic interstate migration vs flows from abroad and Puerto Rico",
       subtitle = "Only domestic interstate flows enter the net figures; the rest are reported separately") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "fig_population_flow_types.png"), p_abroad,
       width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
p_abroad
```

# Year alignment

ACS year *t* interviews run January–December of *t*. Each respondent reports where they lived 12 months before the interview, so ACS *t* covers moves between January *t−1* and December *t*. The move-date distribution is triangular and centred on about 1 January of *t*.

A vehicle yearpair (*t−1*, *t*), with `year` = *t−1*, compares the VIO snapshot of year *t−1* with that of *t*. The repo does not record the Experian snapshot date; it is assumed annual at a fixed point in each year. Whatever that point is, ACS *t* is the best or tied-best match:

| Snapshot date | Centre of the vehicle interval | Best ACS year |
|---|---|---|
| 1 January | 1 July of *t−1* | ACS *t*, tied with ACS *t−1* |
| Mid-year | 1 January of *t* | ACS *t* exactly; ACS *t±1* are 12 months off |
| End of year | 1 July of *t* | ACS *t*, tied with ACS *t+1* |

**Alignment used: ACS year = vehicle `year` + 1.** For example, yearpair 2014/15 (`year` 2014) is paired with ACS 2015.

```{r alignment-table}
alignment <- tibble(year = 2014:2024) |>
  mutate(yearpair = yp_label(year),
         acs_year = year + 1L,
         acs_available = acs_year %in% census_files$acs_year,
         note = case_when(acs_year == 2020 ~ "ACS 2020 1-year tables not released",
                          acs_year == 2025 ~ "ACS 2025 not yet published",
                          .default = ""))
knitr::kable(alignment, caption = "Vehicle yearpair to ACS year")
```

That leaves `r sum(alignment$acs_available)` of 11 vehicle yearpairs with population data: 2019/20 and 2024/25 have none. Every window average below is computed over the **ACS-matched yearpairs only**, for raw and adjusted vehicle flows alike, so raw and adjusted figures always describe the same years. The Tennessee 2014/15 outlier is dropped from averages and regressions, as in `survival.qmd`'s production summaries.

```{r vehicle-load}
vehstock <- read_csv(file.path(surv_data_dir, "state_vehtype_stock_by_year.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

# age-mix accounting counts (survival.qmd production counts): each state's
# age 2-8 survivors minus what national survival would leave from its own
# year-t stock, age by age; they sum to exactly zero nationally per yearpair
agemix <- read_csv(file.path(surv_data_dir, "net_imports_agemix_counts.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

# value = Greene's national-survival-weighted net import rate (the % labels);
# veh_cnt = age-mix count (Sankey widths, regressions, residuals)
veh <- read_csv(file.path(surv_data_dir, "net_imports_long.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(method == "old") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  left_join(vehstock, by = join_by(year, statename, VehicleClass)) |>
  left_join(agemix, by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename, year)) |>
  mutate(veh_cnt  = count_agemix,
         acs_year = year + 1L,
         # survival.qmd drops TN's outlier first yearpair from weighted
         # averages, for counts as well as rates
         excl_tn  = statename == "Tennessee" & year == 2014)
stopifnot(!anyNA(veh$veh_cnt))

net_imports_summary <- read_csv(file.path(surv_data_dir, "net_imports_summary.csv"),
                                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(method == "old")

# pop_use drops the Census-flagged CT 2022, so CT 2021/22 is unmatched
veh_pop <- veh |>
  left_join(pop_use |>
              select(acs_year, statename, pop, pop_net = net,
                     pop_net_rate = net_rate, pop_inflow = inflow,
                     pop_outflow = outflow, from_foreign),
            by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
  mutate(matched = !is.na(pop_net),
         use     = matched & !excl_tn & !is.na(veh_cnt))
```

An empirical check of the alignment: the correlation between state vehicle net-import counts and net domestic migration, pooled over states and years, under the chosen alignment and the two neighbouring ones. All three are computed over the same vehicle years: the years for which all three ACS years exist.

```{r alignment-check}
lag_opts <- c("ACS = year (pop. one year earlier)" = 0L,
              "ACS = year + 1 (used)"              = 1L,
              "ACS = year + 2 (pop. one year later)" = 2L)
avail_acs <- census_files$acs_year
common_years <- (2014:2024)[map_lgl(2014:2024, \(y) all((y + lag_opts) %in% avail_acs))]

align_check <- imap(lag_opts, \(lg, nm) {
  veh |>
    filter(year %in% common_years, !excl_tn, !is.na(veh_cnt)) |>
    mutate(acs_year = year + lg) |>
    inner_join(pop_use |> select(acs_year, statename, pop_net = net),
               by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
    summarise(r = cor(veh_cnt, pop_net),
              slope = sum(veh_cnt * pop_net) / sum(pop_net^2),
              n = n(), .by = VehicleClass) |>
    mutate(alignment = nm)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = VehicleClass, values_from = c(r, slope),
              id_cols = alignment, names_vary = "slowest")
knitr::kable(align_check, digits = 3,
             caption = paste0("Pooled correlation (r) and no-intercept slope of vehicle net-import count on net domestic migration, ",
                              "state x year cells (~305 per class); common vehicle years ",
                              paste(yp_label(common_years), collapse = ", ")))
```

# Sankey helper

This is copied from `survival.qmd` (`sankey-net-flows` chunk) and kept equivalent: exporters → "Net flow pool" → importers, top 15 on each side plus a lumped "Other" node, and link widths drawn from the real, unscaled values. Gross imports versus gross exports goes in the subtitle; nothing is rescaled to balance visually. Node labels read "State (count; rate)". Two additions: `rate_accuracy`, because population rates are much smaller than vehicle rates, and `units_note`, which describes the labels.

```{r sankey-helper}
# df: one row per state, columns STNAME + flow (net imports per yr)
# + rate (net imports as a share of the state's own base, per yr)
make_sankey <- function(df, title_text, units_note, rate_accuracy = 1,
                        flow_word = "imports", out_word = "exports") {
  exporters <- df |>
    filter(flow < 0) |>
    mutate(flow = abs(flow)) |>
    arrange(desc(flow))

  importers <- df |>
    filter(flow > 0) |>
    arrange(desc(flow))

  # top 15 + other
  if (nrow(exporters) > 15) {
    exporters <- bind_rows(
      slice_head(exporters, n = 15),
      tibble(STNAME = "Other exporters",
             flow = sum(exporters$flow[16:nrow(exporters)]),
             rate = NA_real_)
    )
  }
  if (nrow(importers) > 15) {
    importers <- bind_rows(
      slice_head(importers, n = 15),
      tibble(STNAME = "Other importers",
             flow = sum(importers$flow[16:nrow(importers)]),
             rate = NA_real_)
    )
  }

  # gross imports as a share of gross exports across states
  # (top-15 lumping preserves sums)
  actual_balance <- sum(importers$flow) / sum(exporters$flow)

  # link widths are the real, unscaled flows; any gap between gross exports
  # and gross imports is stated in the caption, not rescaled away.
  # "State (count; rate)"; the lumped "Other" nodes pool states with
  # different rates, so count only
  node_labels <- function(d) {
    rate_txt <- if_else(is.na(d$rate), "",
                        paste0("; ", scales::percent(d$rate, accuracy = rate_accuracy)))
    paste0(d$STNAME, " (", scales::comma(round(d$flow, -2)), rate_txt, ")")
  }
  exp_labels <- node_labels(exporters)
  imp_labels <- node_labels(importers)
  pool_label <- "Net flow pool"

  nodes <- tibble(
    name  = c(exp_labels, pool_label, imp_labels),
    group = c(rep("exporter", nrow(exporters)), "pool", rep("importer", nrow(importers)))
  ) |>
    mutate(id = row_number() - 1L)

  pool_id <- nodes |> filter(group == "pool") |> pull(id)

  links <- bind_rows(
    tibble(source = match(exp_labels, nodes$name) - 1L,
           target = pool_id,
           value  = exporters$flow),
    tibble(source = pool_id,
           target = match(imp_labels, nodes$name) - 1L,
           value  = importers$flow)
  )

  color_js <- 'd3.scaleOrdinal().domain(["exporter","pool","importer"]).range(["#7b2d8e","#aaaaaa","#e67e22"])'

  # nodePadding 19 (was 13) keeps the 18px labels of the thinnest nodes
  # (bottom of the exporter column) from overlapping each other
  s <- sankeyNetwork(
    Links = as.data.frame(links), Nodes = as.data.frame(nodes),
    Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value",
    NodeID = "name", NodeGroup = "group", colourScale = color_js,
    fontSize = 18, fontFamily = "sans-serif",
    nodeWidth = 20, nodePadding = 19, sinksRight = TRUE,
    width = 900, height = 900
  )

  balance_note <- paste0(
    "Gross ", flow_word, " = ", scales::percent(actual_balance, accuracy = 0.1),
    " of gross ", out_word, " across states. ", units_note)

  # the widget page is wider than the 920px screenshot, so cap the text width
  # or long titles get cut off at the right edge of the PNG
  text_style <- "max-width:860px; text-align:center; font-family:sans-serif;"
  htmlwidgets::prependContent(
    s,
    htmltools::tags$h3(title_text, style = text_style),
    htmltools::tags$p(balance_note, style = paste(text_style, "color:#555555;"))
  )
}

save_sankey <- function(s, stem) {
  html_file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(stem, ".html"))
  png_file  <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(stem, ".png"))
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(s, file = html_file, selfcontained = TRUE)
  webshot2::webshot(html_file, file = png_file, vwidth = 920, vheight = 1040, delay = 1)
  invisible(png_file)
}

# window bookkeeping: which of a window's yearpairs have ACS data
window_info <- window_years |>
  left_join(alignment |> select(year, acs_available), by = join_by(year)) |>
  summarise(n_total   = n(),
            n_matched = sum(acs_available),
            matched   = list(year[acs_available]),
            missing   = list(year[!acs_available]),
            .by = year_set) |>
  mutate(window_note = map_chr(seq_along(year_set), \(i) {
    miss <- missing[[i]]
    flg  <- census_flags |> filter((acs_year - 1L) %in% matched[[i]])
    paste0(n_matched[i], " of ", n_total[i], " yearpairs in ", year_set_labels[year_set[i]],
           " matched to ACS",
           if (length(miss)) paste0("; no ACS for ", paste(yp_label(miss), collapse = ", ")) else "",
           if (nrow(flg)) paste0("; ", paste0(flg$statename, " excl. ", yp_label(flg$acs_year - 1L),
                                              collapse = ", ")) else "")
  }),
  # vehicle averages also drop Tennessee's outlier 2014/15 (production rule)
  veh_window_note = paste0(window_note,
                           if_else(map_lgl(matched, \(m) 2014L %in% m),
                                   "; Tennessee excl. 2014/15", "")))
knitr::kable(window_info |> select(year_set, n_total, n_matched, veh_window_note))
```

# Population Sankeys

Net domestic migration in persons per year. Population rates are a small fraction of vehicle rates: most states' net migration is within ±1% of population a year. At whole percent most labels would read 0% or ±1%, so **population Sankey labels show the rate to one decimal** ("Florida (…; 1.4%)"). Vehicle and residual Sankeys keep whole percent.

```{r pop-sankeys}
pop_units_note <- "Labels: persons/yr; net domestic migrants as % of state population age 1+ (one decimal)."

# single ACS years (those matched to a vehicle yearpair); Census-flagged
# state-years are left out and named in the title
for (ay in alignment$acs_year[alignment$acs_available]) {
  df <- pop_use |>
    filter(acs_year == ay) |>
    select(STNAME = statename, flow = net, rate = net_rate)
  omitted <- census_flags |> filter(acs_year == ay) |> pull(statename)
  s <- make_sankey(df, paste0(
    "Net domestic migration between states, persons per year (ACS ", ay,
    ": residence now vs 1 year ago, moves ~", ay - 1, "–", ay,
    "; paired with vehicle yearpair ", yp_label(ay - 1),
    if (length(omitted)) paste0("; ", paste(omitted, collapse = ", "),
                                " omitted, Census-flagged processing error") else "",
    ")"),
    pop_units_note, rate_accuracy = 0.1,
    flow_word = "net in-migration", out_word = "net out-migration")
  save_sankey(s, paste0("sankey_population_acs", ay))
}

# averaging windows matching the vehicle windows (ACS-matched years only;
# CT averages its unflagged years)
pop_window <- pop_use |>
  mutate(year = acs_year - 1L) |>
  inner_join(window_years, by = join_by(year), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  summarise(net = mean(net), net_rate = mean(net_rate),
            inflow = mean(inflow), outflow = mean(outflow), pop = mean(pop),
            n_years = n(),
            .by = c(year_set, statename))
write_csv(pop_window, file.path(out_dir, "population_net_migration_window_avg.csv"))

for (ys in names(year_sets)) {
  df <- pop_window |>
    filter(year_set == ys) |>
    select(STNAME = statename, flow = net, rate = net_rate)
  s <- make_sankey(df, paste0(
    "Net domestic migration between states, persons per year (averaged over ",
    window_info$window_note[window_info$year_set == ys], ")"),
    pop_units_note, rate_accuracy = 0.1,
    flow_word = "net in-migration", out_word = "net out-migration")
  save_sankey(s, paste0("sankey_population_", ys))
}
```

```{r show-pop-sankey, out.width = "70%"}
                                                  "sankey_population_acs2022.png")))
```

# Estimating A: vehicles that move per net migrant

The adjustment assumes $\text{vehicle net imports}_{s,c,t} = A_c \times \text{net domestic migration}_{s,t} + \text{market}_{s,c,t}$. Here $A_c$ is the number of age 2-8 vehicles of class *c* that move per net migrant. Vehicle counts are only for age 2-8 vehicles, so $A_c$ concerns that age band only.

## (a) Structural: age 2-8 fleet per capita

**(a1) National.** $A_{c,t} = \sum_s \text{stock}_{s,c,t} / \sum_s \text{pop}_{s,t}$: the national age 2-8 VIO of class *c* in vehicle year *t* over the ACS population age 1+ in the matched ACS year. It varies by year because the class mix shifts: cars fall and SUVs rise.

**(a2) Origin-state ownership.** Each mover carries the per-capita age 2-8 fleet of the state they left:

$$\text{veh}^{pop}_{s} = \sum_j F_{j\to s}\, a_{j} - \text{out}_s\, a_s, \qquad a_j = \text{stock}_{j,c,t}/\text{pop}_{j,t}.$$

This uses the origin–destination matrix. In 2024, in-migrants hidden in suppressed cells are assigned the national ratio. Like the population flows, these sum to zero nationally. Its "effective A" in the table below is the least-squares ratio of these vehicles to net migration.

```{r A-structural}
pop_nat <- pop_state_year |> summarise(pop = sum(pop), .by = acs_year)

A_struct_year <- veh |>
  summarise(stock = sum(stock), .by = c(VehicleClass, year, acs_year)) |>
  inner_join(pop_nat, by = join_by(acs_year)) |>
  mutate(A_struct = stock / pop)

# (a2) origin-state per-capita fleet, carried along each O-D flow
a_state <- vehstock |>
  mutate(acs_year = year + 1L) |>
  inner_join(pop_state_year |> select(acs_year, statename, pop),
             by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
  mutate(a = stock / pop) |>
  select(VehicleClass, year, acs_year, statename, a)

veh_from_pop_od <- dom |>
  filter(!is.na(estimate)) |>
  inner_join(a_state |> rename(origin = statename),
             by = join_by(acs_year, origin), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  rename(statename = dest) |>
  summarise(in_veh = sum(estimate * a), in_alloc = sum(estimate),
            .by = c(VehicleClass, year, acs_year, statename)) |>
  left_join(pop_state_year |> select(acs_year, statename, inflow, outflow),
            by = join_by(acs_year, statename)) |>
  left_join(a_state, by = join_by(VehicleClass, year, acs_year, statename)) |>
  left_join(A_struct_year |> select(VehicleClass, year, A_struct),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, year)) |>
  # 2024 suppressed cells: unallocated in-migrants at the national ratio
  mutate(pop_veh_od = in_veh + (inflow - in_alloc) * A_struct - outflow * a) |>
  select(VehicleClass, year, statename, pop_veh_od)

knitr::kable(
  A_struct_year |>
    select(VehicleClass, yearpair = year, acs_year, A_struct) |>
    mutate(yearpair = yp_label(yearpair)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = VehicleClass, values_from = A_struct),
  digits = 4, caption = "(a1) National age 2-8 vehicles per capita, by matched yearpair")
```

## (b) Empirical: regression slope

$A_c$ is the OLS slope of state vehicle net imports (count) on net domestic migration (persons), pooled over states and ACS-matched yearpairs, with no intercept. The structural model has none: zero migration implies zero population-driven vehicles. Standard errors are clustered by state. Reported alongside:

- the same regression with an intercept;
- a scale factor *k* from regressing vehicle counts on (a1)'s $A_{c,t} \times$ net migration (*k* = 1 means the structural A holds exactly);
- a two-regressor version that adds in-migrants from foreign countries (immigrants buy vehicles on arrival rather than bringing them);
- the slope without the four largest states (CA, NY, FL, TX), which dominate a count regression;
- a rate form: vehicle net-import rate on net-migration rate, which weights states equally. If every state's per-capita fleet equalled the national one, (a1) would predict a slope of exactly 1;
- a slope for each year separately.

Net domestic migration sums to zero across states each year, so its pooled mean is about zero. The with-intercept slope is therefore practically identical to the no-intercept slope; the intercept only absorbs the small non-zero mean of vehicle net imports.

```{r A-empirical}
# OLS with state-clustered (CR0) standard errors; returns the last coefficient
fit_slope <- function(y, X, cluster) {
  X <- as.matrix(X)
  XtX_inv <- solve(crossprod(X))
  b <- XtX_inv %*% crossprod(X, y)
  e <- as.vector(y - X %*% b)
  meat <- split(seq_along(y), cluster) |>
    map(\(i) tcrossprod(crossprod(X[i, , drop = FALSE], e[i]))) |>
    reduce(`+`)
  V <- XtX_inv %*% meat %*% XtX_inv
  has_int <- all(X[, 1] == 1)
  tibble(term = colnames(X),
         A    = as.vector(b),
         se   = sqrt(diag(V)),
         r2   = if (has_int) 1 - sum(e^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2) else 1 - sum(e^2) / sum(y^2),
         n    = length(y))
}

reg_data <- veh_pop |>
  filter(use) |>
  left_join(A_struct_year |> select(VehicleClass, year, A_struct),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, year))

A_emp_fits <- reg_data |>
  nest(.by = VehicleClass) |>
  mutate(fits = map(data, \(d) bind_rows(
    "(b) through origin" =
      fit_slope(d$veh_cnt, cbind(pop_net = d$pop_net), d$statename),
    "(b) with intercept" =
      fit_slope(d$veh_cnt, cbind(int = 1, pop_net = d$pop_net), d$statename) |>
        filter(term == "pop_net"),
    "(b) k on structural A x pop" =
      fit_slope(d$veh_cnt, cbind(k = d$A_struct * d$pop_net), d$statename),
    "(b) + foreign in-migrants" = with(
      filter(d, !is.na(from_foreign)),   # 2024 suppresses a few foreign cells
      fit_slope(veh_cnt, cbind(pop_net = pop_net, from_foreign = from_foreign), statename)),
    "(b) excl. CA, NY, FL, TX" = with(
      filter(d, !statename %in% c("California", "New York", "Florida", "Texas")),
      fit_slope(veh_cnt, cbind(pop_net = pop_net), statename)),
    # rate form weights states equally; (a1) predicts a slope of 1 here
    # (vehicle rate = A * pop_net / stock = pop_net / pop when A = stock / pop).
    # Uses Greene's weighted rate, so it does not depend on the count basis
    "(b) rate form: vehicle rate on pop. rate" = with(
      filter(d, !is.na(value)),
      fit_slope(value, cbind(int = 1, pop_net_rate = pop_net_rate), statename) |>
        filter(term == "pop_net_rate")),
    .id = "spec"))) |>
  select(VehicleClass, fits) |>
  unnest(fits)

A_emp <- A_emp_fits |>
  filter(spec == "(b) through origin") |>
  select(VehicleClass, A_emp = A, A_emp_se = se)

# per-year cross-section slopes (through origin)
A_emp_year <- reg_data |>
  nest(.by = c(VehicleClass, year)) |>
  mutate(fit = map(data, \(d) fit_slope(d$veh_cnt, cbind(pop_net = d$pop_net), d$statename))) |>
  select(VehicleClass, year, fit) |>
  unnest(fit)
```

```{r A-table}
A_struct_mean <- A_struct_year |>
  filter(year %in% reg_data$year) |>
  summarise(A = mean(A_struct), lo = min(A_struct), hi = max(A_struct), .by = VehicleClass)

# effective A of (a2): least-squares ratio of its vehicles to net migration
A_od_eff <- reg_data |>
  left_join(veh_from_pop_od, by = join_by(VehicleClass, year, statename)) |>
  summarise(A = sum(pop_veh_od * pop_net) / sum(pop_net^2), .by = VehicleClass)

A_table <- bind_rows(
  A_struct_mean |> mutate(spec = "(a1) structural, national per capita (mean over matched years)",
                          note = paste0("range ", round(lo, 3), "–", round(hi, 3))),
  A_od_eff |> mutate(spec = "(a2) structural, origin-state per capita (effective)", note = ""),
  A_emp_fits |>
    filter(!(spec == "(b) + foreign in-migrants" & term == "from_foreign")) |>
    transmute(VehicleClass, spec, A, note = paste0(
      "SE ", signif(se, 2), "; R2 ", round(r2, 3), "; n ", n,
      case_when(spec == "(b) k on structural A x pop" ~ " (k is a multiplier, not A)",
                str_detect(spec, "rate form") ~ " (slope in rate terms; (a1) implies 1)",
                .default = ""))),
  A_emp_fits |>
    filter(spec == "(b) + foreign in-migrants", term == "from_foreign") |>
    transmute(VehicleClass, spec = "(b) + foreign in-migrants: foreign coef.", A,
              note = paste0("SE ", signif(se, 2)))
) |>
  select(VehicleClass, spec, A, note) |>
  arrange(factor(VehicleClass, classes))
write_csv(A_table, file.path(out_dir, "A_estimates.csv"))

A_table |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = VehicleClass, values_from = c(A, note), names_vary = "slowest") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Estimates of A (age 2-8 vehicles per net domestic migrant)")
```

```{r A-by-year, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
p_Ayear <- A_emp_year |>
  select(VehicleClass, year, A, se) |>
  mutate(spec = "(b) empirical slope, single year") |>
  bind_rows(A_struct_year |>
              filter(year %in% reg_data$year) |>
              transmute(VehicleClass, year, A = A_struct, se = NA_real_,
                        spec = "(a1) structural per capita") |>
              # explicit NA year so the line breaks at unmatched 2019/20
              complete(VehicleClass, spec, year = 2014:2023)) |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, classes)) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, A, colour = spec)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = A - 1.96 * se, ymax = A + 1.96 * se),
                  data = \(d) filter(d, !is.na(se)), size = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = \(d) filter(d, is.na(se)), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, is.na(se)), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = A_emp), data = A_emp |>
               mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, classes)),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = col_imp) +
  facet_wrap(~VehicleClass, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("(a1) structural per capita" = "#2c7fb8",
                                 "(b) empirical slope, single year" = col_imp)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2014, 2024, 2), labels = yp_label) +
  labs(x = "Vehicle yearpair", y = "A (age 2-8 vehicles per net migrant)", colour = NULL,
       title = "A by year: structural per-capita fleet vs single-year empirical slopes",
       subtitle = "Dashed: pooled empirical slope; bars: ±1.96 state-clustered SE") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# How much of vehicle net migration population explains

Two measures:

- **Explained share.** $1 - \sum \text{resid}^2 / \sum \text{veh}^2$, the uncentred R² of the no-intercept model, over state × year cells and over the 51 window averages. It is negative when subtracting $A \times$ pop makes the vehicle flows *larger* in squared terms than they were.
- **Magnitude ratio.** $\sum |A \cdot \text{pop}_{net}| / \sum |\text{veh}|$: the size of population-attributable vehicle flows relative to all vehicle net flows.

The curve shows the explained share as a function of A. Its maximum is at the empirical slope (b), by construction.

```{r residuals}
A_methods <- c(struct_nat = "(a1) structural, national per capita",
               struct_od  = "(a2) structural, origin-state per capita",
               empirical  = "(b) empirical slope")

veh_adj <- veh_pop |>
  left_join(A_struct_year |> select(VehicleClass, year, A_struct), by = join_by(VehicleClass, year)) |>
  left_join(A_emp |> select(VehicleClass, A_emp), by = join_by(VehicleClass)) |>
  left_join(veh_from_pop_od, by = join_by(VehicleClass, year, statename)) |>
  filter(matched) |>
  mutate(struct_nat = A_struct * pop_net,
         struct_od  = pop_veh_od,
         empirical  = A_emp * pop_net) |>
  pivot_longer(c(struct_nat, struct_od, empirical), names_to = "A_method", values_to = "pop_veh") |>
  # residual % keeps Greene's weighted rate as the base: rate minus the
  # population-attributable share of the state's age 2-8 stock
  mutate(resid_cnt    = veh_cnt - pop_veh,
         pop_veh_rate = pop_veh / stock,
         resid_rate   = value - pop_veh_rate)

write_csv(veh_adj |>
            select(A_method, VehicleClass, statename, year, yearpair, acs_year, excl_tn,
                   stock, value, veh_cnt_agemix = veh_cnt, pop, pop_net, pop_net_rate,
                   pop_veh, pop_veh_rate, resid_cnt, resid_rate),
          file.path(out_dir, "vehicle_pop_adjusted_by_state_class_year.csv"))

# window averages over ACS-matched yearpairs (TN 2014/15 excluded, as in the
# production summaries); Average_* from net_imports_summary are the full-window
# raw values for reference
adj_window <- veh_adj |>
  filter(use) |>
  inner_join(window_years, by = join_by(year), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  # rates na.rm like survival.qmd's Average: DC Pickup 2016/17 has a count
  # but no weighted rate
  summarise(raw_cnt      = mean(veh_cnt),
            raw_rate     = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            pop_net      = mean(pop_net),
            pop_net_rate = mean(pop_net_rate),
            pop_veh      = mean(pop_veh),
            resid_cnt    = mean(resid_cnt),
            resid_rate   = mean(resid_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_years      = n(),
            .by = c(A_method, year_set, VehicleClass, statename)) |>
  left_join(net_imports_summary |>
              select(year_set, VehicleClass, statename,
                     raw_cnt_full_window = Average_agemix, raw_rate_full_window = Average),
            by = join_by(year_set, VehicleClass, statename)) |>
  mutate(rank_raw   = rank(-raw_cnt),
         rank_resid = rank(-resid_cnt),
         rank_change = rank_raw - rank_resid,
         .by = c(A_method, year_set, VehicleClass))
write_csv(adj_window, file.path(out_dir, "vehicle_pop_adjusted_window_avg.csv"))
```

```{r explained}
share_fun <- function(veh, pop_veh) {
  tibble(explained_share = 1 - sum((veh - pop_veh)^2) / sum(veh^2),
         magnitude_ratio = sum(abs(pop_veh)) / sum(abs(veh)),
         sign_agree      = mean(sign(veh) == sign(pop_veh)))
}

explained <- bind_rows(
  veh_adj |>
    filter(use) |>
    reframe(share_fun(veh_cnt, pop_veh), .by = c(A_method, VehicleClass)) |>
    mutate(level = "state x year"),
  adj_window |>
    reframe(share_fun(raw_cnt, pop_veh), .by = c(A_method, VehicleClass, year_set)) |>
    mutate(level = paste0("window avg: ", year_set))
) |>
  mutate(A_method = A_methods[A_method]) |>
  relocate(level, A_method, VehicleClass)
write_csv(explained, file.path(out_dir, "explained_share.csv"))

explained |>
  filter(level %in% c("state x year", "window avg: yrs_all", "window avg: yrs1519")) |>
  arrange(level, A_method, factor(VehicleClass, classes)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Share of vehicle net-flow variation accounted for by A x net domestic migration")
```

# Population-adjusted vehicle Sankeys

The residual is vehicle net imports minus $A \times$ net domestic migration, averaged over the ACS-matched yearpairs of each window. There is one set of Sankeys for each A: (a1) structural national (`struct_nat`), (a2) structural origin-state (`struct_od`) and (b) empirical (`empirical`). Raw vehicle Sankeys over the same matched yearpairs are also rendered (`sankey_vehicle_raw_*_matched`), so raw and adjusted can be compared like for like. The full-window raw Sankeys are in `survival.qmd`'s outputs.

Labels follow `survival.qmd`'s production hybrid:

- **Counts and ribbon widths** are age-mix accounting counts.
- **%** is Greene's national-survival-weighted net import rate, which is age-standardized.
- **Residual Sankeys:** the count is the age-mix count minus A × net migrants. The % is the weighted rate minus A × net migrants as a share of the state's age 2-8 stock, to the whole percent.

Age-mix counts sum to zero nationally in every yearpair, and so does A × net migration under (a1) and (b). Any import/export gap in these Sankeys therefore comes from state-specific exclusions: Tennessee 2014/15 (production rule) and Connecticut 2021/22 (Census-flagged ACS 2022). Under (a2), the national ratio given to 2024's suppressed in-migrant cells also adds a small gap.

```{r residual-sankeys}
# same wording as survival.qmd's production Sankeys; age-mix counts and
# A x net migration each sum to ~zero nationally per yearpair, so any
# import/export gap comes from the state exclusions named in the title
gap_note <- " Any gap between imports and exports comes from the state exclusions named in the title."
veh_units_note <- paste0(
  "Labels: vehicles/yr, each state's survivors counted age by age against national survival; ",
  "% = net import rate with national-survival weights, of the state's own age 2-8 stock per year.",
  gap_note)
resid_units_note <- paste0(
  "Labels: vehicles/yr, each state's survivors counted age by age against national survival, ",
  "minus A × net domestic migrants; % = net import rate with national-survival weights minus ",
  "A × net migrants, both as a share of the state's own age 2-8 stock per year.",
  gap_note)
A_label <- function(m, vc) {
  if (m == "struct_nat") {
    a <- A_struct_mean |> filter(VehicleClass == vc)
    paste0("A = (a1) national per capita, ",
           sprintf("%.3f", a$lo), "–", sprintf("%.3f", a$hi), " by year")
  } else if (m == "struct_od") {
    paste0("A = (a2) origin-state per capita, effective ",
           sprintf("%.3f", A_od_eff$A[A_od_eff$VehicleClass == vc]))
  } else {
    paste0("A = (b) empirical slope, ",
           sprintf("%.3f", A_emp$A_emp[A_emp$VehicleClass == vc]))
  }
}

for (ys in names(year_sets)) {
  wnote <- window_info$veh_window_note[window_info$year_set == ys]
  for (vc in classes) {
    raw_df <- adj_window |>
      filter(A_method == "struct_nat", year_set == ys, VehicleClass == vc) |>
      select(STNAME = statename, flow = raw_cnt, rate = raw_rate)
    s <- make_sankey(raw_df, paste0(
      "Net Export and Import of ", vc, "s per year (age 2-8 vehicles; averaged over ",
      wnote, "). Includes vehicle movements associated with both population migration and vehicle markets."),
      veh_units_note)
    save_sankey(s, paste0("sankey_vehicle_raw_", str_to_lower(vc), "_", ys, "_matched"))

    for (m in c("struct_nat", "struct_od", "empirical")) {
      df <- adj_window |>
        filter(A_method == m, year_set == ys, VehicleClass == vc) |>
        select(STNAME = statename, flow = resid_cnt, rate = resid_rate)
      s <- make_sankey(df, paste0(
        "Population-adjusted Net Export and Import of ", vc,
        "s per year (age 2-8 vehicles; net imports minus A × net domestic migrants, ",
        A_label(m, vc), " ", str_to_lower(vc), "s/person; averaged over ", wnote, ")"),
        resid_units_note)
      save_sankey(s, paste0("sankey_residual_", str_to_lower(vc), "_", ys, "_", m))
    }
  }
}
```

```{r rankings, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 13}
plot_dumbbell <- function(ys) {
  d <- adj_window |>

    pivot_wider(names_from = A_method, values_from = resid_cnt) |>

  d |>
    ggplot(aes(y = st)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
    geom_segment(aes(x = raw_cnt, xend = struct_nat, yend = st), colour = "grey70") +
    geom_point(aes(x = raw_cnt, colour = "raw"), size = 1.8) +
    geom_point(aes(x = struct_nat, colour = "adjusted, (a1) structural"), size = 1.8) +
    geom_point(aes(x = struct_od, colour = "adjusted, (a2) origin-state"), size = 1.2, shape = 4) +
    geom_point(aes(x = empirical, colour = "adjusted, (b) empirical"), size = 1.8, shape = 17) +
    facet_wrap(~VehicleClass, scales = "free", nrow = 1) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) str_remove(x, "___.*$")) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("raw" = "grey30",
                                   "adjusted, (a1) structural" = "#2c7fb8",
                                   "adjusted, (a2) origin-state" = "#41ab5d",
                                   "adjusted, (b) empirical" = col_imp)) +
    labs(x = "Net imports (age 2-8 vehicles/yr)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
         title = "Vehicle net imports by state: raw vs population-adjusted",
         subtitle = paste0("States ordered by raw value; averages over ",
                           window_info$veh_window_note[window_info$year_set == ys])) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
}
# order states within each facet (no tidytext dependency)
tidytext_reorder <- function(x, by, within) {
  key <- paste(x, within, sep = "___")
  factor(key, levels = unique(key[order(within, by)]))
}

for (ys in c("yrs_all", "yrs1519")) {
  p <- plot_dumbbell(ys)
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("fig_rankings_raw_vs_adjusted_", ys, ".png")), p,
         width = 13, height = 13, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
}
plot_dumbbell("yrs_all")
```

# Sensitivity to A

Each state's adjusted window average as A scales from 0 to 2 × the (a1) structural value. The (b) empirical A corresponds to a multiplier of *k* = A(b) / mean A(a1), marked by the dashed line. Labelled states have the largest raw flows or the largest net migration.

```{r sensitivity, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5.5}
sens <- veh_adj |>
  filter(A_method == "struct_nat", use, year %in% year_sets$yrs_all) |>
  select(VehicleClass, statename, year, veh_cnt, pop_veh) |>
  cross_join(tibble(mult = seq(0, 2, by = 0.1))) |>
  summarise(resid = mean(veh_cnt - mult * pop_veh), .by = c(VehicleClass, statename, mult))

k_emp <- A_emp |>
  left_join(A_struct_mean |> select(VehicleClass, A), by = join_by(VehicleClass)) |>
  mutate(k = A_emp / A, VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, classes))

lab_states <- adj_window |>
  filter(year_set == "yrs_all", A_method == "struct_nat") |>
  filter(rank(-abs(raw_cnt)) <= 6 | rank(-abs(pop_net)) <= 5, .by = VehicleClass) |>
  select(VehicleClass, statename)

p_sens <- sens |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, classes)) |>
  ggplot(aes(mult, resid, group = statename)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = \(d) semi_join(d, lab_states |> mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, classes)),
                                    by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename)),
            colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = statename),
                  data = \(d) d |> filter(mult == 2) |>
                    semi_join(lab_states |> mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, classes)),
                              by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename)),
                  size = 2.8, direction = "y", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.05,
                  min.segment.length = 0, max.overlaps = 30) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "#2c7fb8") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = k), data = k_emp, colour = col_imp, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~VehicleClass, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 2.5), breaks = seq(0, 2, 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "A as a multiple of (a1) structural per-capita fleet",
       y = "Adjusted net imports (vehicles/yr)",
       title = "Sensitivity of population-adjusted vehicle net imports to A",
       subtitle = "All ACS-matched yearpairs. Solid blue: (a1) structural; dashed orange: (b) empirical")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "fig_sensitivity_to_A_yrs_all.png"), p_sens,
       width = 12, height = 5.5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
p_sens
```

The adjusted value is linear in A, so each state's sign flips at a single multiplier: raw / (population-attributable at (a1)). The table lists the states whose sign flips somewhere between 0 and 2 × (a1).

```{r sign-dependence}
sign_dep <- veh_adj |>
  filter(A_method == "struct_nat", use, year %in% year_sets$yrs_all) |>
  summarise(raw_cnt = mean(veh_cnt), pop_veh_a1 = mean(pop_veh),
            .by = c(VehicleClass, statename)) |>
  mutate(flips_at_multiple = raw_cnt / pop_veh_a1) |>
  filter(flips_at_multiple > 0, flips_at_multiple <= 2) |>
  left_join(k_emp |> transmute(VehicleClass = as.character(VehicleClass), k_empirical = k),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass)) |>
  arrange(factor(VehicleClass, classes), flips_at_multiple)
knitr::kable(sign_dep |> mutate(across(c(raw_cnt, pop_veh_a1), \(x) round(x, -2))),
             digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "States whose adjusted sign depends on A (all matched yearpairs): sign flips at A = flips_at_multiple × (a1); k_empirical = A(b) / mean A(a1)")
```

# Vehicle count basis: age-mix accounting vs rate × stock

The first version of this analysis converted Greene's weighted rate to a count as rate × that year's age 2-8 stock. Production `survival.qmd` (PR #3) now uses age-mix accounting counts, and so does everything above. For reference, the key statistics on both bases are below, over the same state × yearpair cells (rate × stock drops DC Pickup 2016/17, which has no rate).

```{r count-basis}
basis_cmp <- veh_pop |>
  filter(use) |>
  left_join(A_struct_year |> select(VehicleClass, year, A_struct),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, year)) |>
  mutate(`age-mix accounting` = veh_cnt, `rate x stock` = value * stock) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`age-mix accounting`, `rate x stock`),
               names_to = "count_basis", values_to = "cnt") |>
  filter(!is.na(cnt)) |>
  summarise(gross_flow   = sum(abs(cnt)) / n_distinct(year) / 2,
            A_b          = sum(cnt * pop_net) / sum(pop_net^2),
            explained_a1 = 1 - sum((cnt - A_struct * pop_net)^2) / sum(cnt^2),
            explained_b  = 1 - sum((cnt - A_b * pop_net)^2) / sum(cnt^2),
            .by = c(VehicleClass, count_basis)) |>
  arrange(factor(VehicleClass, classes), count_basis)
write_csv(basis_cmp, file.path(out_dir, "count_basis_comparison.csv"))
knitr::kable(basis_cmp, digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "Key statistics by vehicle count basis (state x yearpair cells; gross_flow = mean yearly sum of |count| / 2)")

basis_wide <- basis_cmp |>
  select(VehicleClass, count_basis, A_b, explained_a1) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = count_basis, values_from = c(A_b, explained_a1))
basis_val <- \(col, vc) sprintf("%.3f", basis_wide[[col]][basis_wide$VehicleClass == vc])
```

The structural A and the rate-form slopes do not depend on the count basis. The two count bases correlate at about 0.99 state by state, so the switch moves little:

- **(b) empirical slope:** SUVs go from `r basis_val("A_b_rate x stock", "SUV")` to `r basis_val("A_b_age-mix accounting", "SUV")`. Cars (`r basis_val("A_b_rate x stock", "Car")` → `r basis_val("A_b_age-mix accounting", "Car")`) and pickups (`r basis_val("A_b_rate x stock", "Pickup")` → `r basis_val("A_b_age-mix accounting", "Pickup")`) barely change.
- **Explained shares** shift by at most about two percentage points.

# Discussion

```{r disc-values, echo = FALSE}
f3  <- \(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
f2  <- \(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
pct <- \(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 1)
by_class <- \(df, col) df |> select(VehicleClass, value = {{ col }}) |> deframe()

A1     <- by_class(A_struct_mean, A)
A1_lo  <- by_class(A_struct_mean, lo)
A1_hi  <- by_class(A_struct_mean, hi)
Aod    <- by_class(A_od_eff, A)
fits   <- \(sp) A_emp_fits |> filter(spec == sp, term != "from_foreign")
Ab     <- by_class(fits("(b) through origin"), A)
Ab_se  <- by_class(fits("(b) through origin"), se)
k_b    <- by_class(fits("(b) k on structural A x pop"), A)
Ab_ex4 <- by_class(fits("(b) excl. CA, NY, FL, TX"), A)
b_rate <- by_class(fits("(b) rate form: vehicle rate on pop. rate"), A)
b_for  <- A_emp_fits |>
  filter(spec == "(b) + foreign in-migrants", term == "from_foreign") |>
  by_class(A)
yr_lo  <- by_class(A_emp_year |> summarise(v = min(A), .by = VehicleClass), v)
yr_hi  <- by_class(A_emp_year |> summarise(v = max(A), .by = VehicleClass), v)

ex <- \(lvl, m, col = "explained_share") explained |>
  filter(level == lvl, A_method == A_methods[[m]]) |>
  select(VehicleClass, value = all_of(col)) |>
  deframe()
ex_sy_a1 <- ex("state x year", "struct_nat"); ex_sy_b <- ex("state x year", "empirical")
ex_w_a1  <- ex("window avg: yrs_all", "struct_nat"); ex_w_b <- ex("window avg: yrs_all", "empirical")
mag_a1   <- ex("state x year", "struct_nat", "magnitude_ratio")

rc_a1 <- rank_corr |> filter(A_method == A_methods[["struct_nat"]]) |> pull(spearman_raw_vs_adjusted)
rc_b  <- rank_corr |> filter(A_method == A_methods[["empirical"]]) |> pull(spearman_raw_vs_adjusted)
r_align <- align_check |> select(starts_with("r_")) |> unlist()

top_resid <- \(vc, side, n = 4) adj_window |>
  filter(year_set == "yrs_all", A_method == "struct_nat", VehicleClass == vc) |>
  slice_max(if (side == "imp") resid_cnt else -resid_cnt, n = n) |>
  pull(statename) |>
  paste(collapse = ", ")

moe_stats <- pop_use |>
  filter(acs_year %in% alignment$acs_year[alignment$acs_available]) |>
  summarise(med_rel = median(net_moe / abs(net)), within = mean(abs(net) < net_moe))

ca_flip <- sign_dep |> filter(statename == "California", VehicleClass == "Car") |> pull(flips_at_multiple)
```

**Year alignment.** ACS year = vehicle `year` + 1 is the alignment used throughout. The empirical check gives pooled correlations between `r f2(min(r_align))` and `r f2(max(r_align))` across the three candidate alignments, rising slightly toward later ACS years. State migration patterns persist strongly from year to year, so this check cannot discriminate sharply. The slight preference for later ACS years fits a late-in-year Experian snapshot. With an end-of-year snapshot (registrations as of about 1 January of *t+1*), ACS *t+1* (vehicle `year` + 2) is as close as ACS *t*. That alignment would raise the empirical slopes by about a fifth (see the alignment table) and leave (a1) essentially unchanged. The snapshot date in the Experian documentation would settle this.

**Population migration.** Net domestic migration is concentrated: over all matched years the largest net losses are `r pop_window |> filter(year_set == "yrs_all") |> slice_min(net, n = 4) |> pull(statename) |> paste(collapse = ", ")` and the largest gains `r pop_window |> filter(year_set == "yrs_all") |> slice_max(net, n = 4) |> pull(statename) |> paste(collapse = ", ")`. ACS 2021–2022 (moves during 2020–2022) show the pandemic-era surge: the sum of state net gains rose from ~0.75 million to over 1 million persons a year. Single-year state net migration is noisy. The median 90% MOE is `r pct(moe_stats$med_rel)` of the absolute net value, and `r pct(moe_stats$within)` of state-years have a net figure smaller than its MOE. Window averages are much more reliable than single years.

**A estimates.**

- **(a1) national per capita:** `r f3(A1["Car"])` cars (`r f3(A1_lo["Car"])`–`r f3(A1_hi["Car"])` by year, falling as cars leave the fleet), `r f3(A1["SUV"])` SUVs (`r f3(A1_lo["SUV"])`–`r f3(A1_hi["SUV"])`, rising) and `r f3(A1["Pickup"])` pickups per net migrant.
- **(a2) origin-state ownership:** effectively `r f3(Aod["Car"])`, `r f3(Aod["SUV"])` and `r f3(Aod["Pickup"])`. Pickups fall furthest. Much of the net migration leaves low-pickup states (CA, NY, IL, NJ), so in-migrants elsewhere bring fewer pickups per person than the national average, while out-migrants from high-pickup states take more.
- **(b) empirical pooled slope:** `r f3(Ab["Car"])` ± `r f3(Ab_se["Car"])` (car), `r f3(Ab["SUV"])` ± `r f3(Ab_se["SUV"])` (SUV) and `r f3(Ab["Pickup"])` ± `r f3(Ab_se["Pickup"])` (pickup), with state-clustered SEs. That is *k* = `r f2(k_b["Car"])`, `r f2(k_b["SUV"])` and `r f2(k_b["Pickup"])` times (a1). The SEs are 50–100% of the estimates, so the data cannot statistically separate (b) from (a1) or, for pickups, from zero. Single-year slopes range from `r f3(yr_lo["Car"])` to `r f3(yr_hi["Car"])` for cars.

**Which A is more defensible.** (a1) is the more defensible basis for the adjustment, and (b) is best read as a sensitivity bound, for four reasons:

1. **(a1) is an accounting statement under one explicit assumption,** that each net migrant takes the average age 2-8 fleet with them. (b) is a fitted slope, so it absorbs *any* vehicle flow correlated with migration. Dealers and auctions shifting used inventory toward fast-growing states would load onto (b), yet that is market behaviour, the very thing the adjustment is meant to isolate. By construction (b) maximises the "explained" share, so it over-attributes to population.
2. **(b) rests on a few states.** A count regression is dominated by CA, NY, FL and TX. Florida is the largest net population importer yet a large vehicle net exporter, which pulls the slope down; New York pulls the other way. Dropping those four states moves the slope to `r f3(Ab_ex4["Car"])` / `r f3(Ab_ex4["SUV"])` / `r f3(Ab_ex4["Pickup"])`.
3. **The size-neutral rate form agrees with (a1).** Regressing vehicle net-import rates on net-migration rates gives slopes of `r f2(b_rate["Car"])`, `r f2(b_rate["SUV"])` and `r f2(b_rate["Pickup"])`, close to the value of 1 that (a1) implies, for all three classes.
4. **(a1) is, if anything, an upper bound on vehicles physically moving with people.** Movers are younger and more often renters, so they own fewer vehicles than average, and some sell before moving and buy at the destination. The resale itself is a market transaction within each state and does not show up as an interstate flow.

**Pickups are the exception: (a2) is the more defensible structural variant there.** Pickup ownership per capita varies several-fold across states. The national ratio therefore over-adjusts states whose movers own few pickups: California turns from a pickup net exporter into a net importer under (a1), but stays near its raw value under (a2). (a2) also accounts for more of the pickup variation (`r pct(ex("state x year", "struct_od")["Pickup"])` of state × year cells, against `r pct(ex_sy_a1["Pickup"])` for (a1)). (a2) has its own extreme case. It assumes people moving into DC bring their origin state's pickups, which leaves DC with a pickup residual of `r pct(adj_window |> filter(A_method == "struct_od", year_set == "yrs_all", VehicleClass == "Pickup", statename == "District of Columbia") |> pull(resid_rate))` of its very small stock. For cars and SUVs, (a1) and (a2) give similar effective A and explained shares.

**How much vehicle net migration population explains.** Measured by the uncentred R² over state × year cells, net domestic migration × A accounts for:

| A | Car | SUV | Pickup |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a1) | `r pct(ex_sy_a1["Car"])` | `r pct(ex_sy_a1["SUV"])` | `r pct(ex_sy_a1["Pickup"])` |
| (b) | `r pct(ex_sy_b["Car"])` | `r pct(ex_sy_b["SUV"])` | `r pct(ex_sy_b["Pickup"])` |

Over the all-years window averages the shares are `r pct(ex_w_a1["Car"])` / `r pct(ex_w_a1["SUV"])` / `r pct(ex_w_a1["Pickup"])` with (a1) and `r pct(ex_w_b["Car"])` / `r pct(ex_w_b["SUV"])` / `r pct(ex_w_b["Pickup"])` with (b). In magnitude, the population-attributable vehicle flows under (a1) equal about `r pct(mean(mag_a1))` of gross vehicle net flows.

Population migration is therefore a real but minority component of the survival-difference vehicle flows: roughly a quarter of their size, and a tenth to a quarter of their variation for cars and SUVs, less for pickups. The dominant patterns survive the adjustment:

- the largest population-adjusted (a1) net exporters are `r top_resid("Car", "exp")` for cars and `r top_resid("Pickup", "exp")` for pickups;
- the largest net importers are `r top_resid("Car", "imp")` for cars and `r top_resid("SUV", "imp")` for SUVs.

Several residual exporters (NY/NJ, FL, TX, LA, PA) have major vehicle-export ports. That fits two things this survival-difference method cannot separate from interstate migration: international used-vehicle exports and state differences in scrappage. That is a hypothesis, not tested here. The foreign-in-migrant coefficient in the two-regressor fit is negative (`r f3(b_for["Car"])` cars per foreign in-migrant). This reflects the same coastal pattern; it is not a causal effect of immigration.

**Which states change.** The states that move are those with the largest net migration: California, New York, Illinois and New Jersey on the out-migration side, Florida, Texas, Arizona and North Carolina on the in-migration side. Adding back their out-migration makes California and Illinois close to neutral: California's car flow changes sign at `r f2(ca_flip)` × (a1), between the (a1) and (b) values. Removing in-migration pushes Texas and Arizona car and SUV flows to or further below zero, and makes Florida the largest car net exporter. Overall rankings change little. Spearman correlations between raw and adjusted window averages are `r f2(min(rc_a1))`–`r f2(max(rc_a1))` with (a1) and `r f2(min(rc_b))`–`r f2(max(rc_b))` with (b).

**Caveats.**

- ACS flows are survey estimates with large MOEs for small states.
- The 2024 table suppresses small cells (2024 totals come from the complete supplemental sheets).
- Connecticut's 2022 data are excluded because of Census's flagged processing error. Other states' 2022 out-migration to CT is slightly overstated; see the check table.
- 2019/20 and 2024/25 have no ACS match.
- ACS cannot see emigration, and only domestic interstate moves are adjusted for.
- A uses persons age 1+, not households or licensed drivers.
- Matched-year raw averages differ slightly from `survival.qmd`'s full-window averages because they omit 2019/20 and 2024/25. They are kept so that raw and adjusted figures cover identical years.

# Outputs

All in `est net flows/population/` (git-ignored):

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `census_state_to_state_flows.csv` | Tidy ACS flows: acs_year × origin × destination, estimate, MOE, suppressed flag (incl. Puerto Rico, U.S. Island Areas, foreign country) |
| `census_state_totals.csv` | Population, same-house, same-state, in-migrant, from-abroad totals (+ 2024 out-migrant totals) |
| `population_net_migration_by_state_year.csv` | Inflow, outflow, net (persons), MOEs, net rate, from-abroad components, moves to PR |
| `population_net_migration_window_avg.csv` | Window averages over ACS-matched years |
| `A_estimates.csv` | All A estimates |
| `vehicle_pop_adjusted_by_state_class_year.csv` | Raw (age-mix) count and weighted rate, population-attributable and residual counts and rates, per A method |
| `vehicle_pop_adjusted_window_avg.csv` | The same averaged over each window's matched yearpairs, with ranks and the full-window raw values |
| `explained_share.csv`, `biggest_changes_yrs_all.csv` | Explained-share and largest-change tables |
| `count_basis_comparison.csv` | A(b) and explained shares on age-mix vs rate × stock counts |
| `sankey_population_acs<year>.*`, `sankey_population_<window>.*` | Population Sankeys |
| `sankey_vehicle_raw_<class>_<window>_matched.*` | Raw vehicle Sankeys over ACS-matched yearpairs |
| `sankey_residual_<class>_<window>_<struct_nat\|struct_od\|empirical>.*` | Population-adjusted vehicle Sankeys, by A |
| `fig_*.png` | Figures above |
